rebuttal.text: Going concern is not a risk factor here, it is the operating model: Note 2 (p.9) says management does not anticipate positive operating cash flow in the near future, and the balance sheet (p.2-3) shows $220,275 of cash against $58.9M of current liabilities. The share count went from 267,872,804 at Feb 28 to 596,259,245 at Aug 31 to 861,808,211 on the Oct 20 cover: that is 3.2x in under eight months after a 1-for-100 reverse split (p.3, p.49, cover). The pitch's target of 0.0030 assumes the denominator stops moving. It has never stopped. Series F preferred converts into 3.45 times the entire outstanding float at the holder's option (p.48). Any re-rating Lulu hopes for is the trigger for that conversion. The convertibles price at 65% of the three lowest trades of the prior ten days (p.62) and a $10M equity purchase agreement sits against a market cap under $1M (p.49). The PRE 14C to lift authorized shares from 12B to 27B is the company telling you what comes next. The 'breakeven' catalyst is a press release about monthly operating cash, not GAAP, and it is silent on the $12.8M of accrued interest and the deferred variable payment obligations (p.2). Breakeven before debt service is not solvency. Liquidity: a $2,000 ticket is about 1.8M shares in a name that trades ~$55k a day with a bid-ask of 0.0010/0.0011, a 10% spread. The paper fill at the ask starts the trade down 10% before anything happens.
